To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

DNA G-quadruplexes can be biotinylates by hemin-catalyzed peroxidase activity, with good discrimination between quadruplex and duplex, and with the resulting biotinylate being amenable to polymerization chain reaction amplification and analysis by ChIP-seq.

DNA and RNA G-quadrupplexes can self-biotinylate in vitro via the intrinsic peroxidase catalytic activity of hemin bound to them, and that this reaction is highly specific for G-quartets and can be exploited for labeling and identifying G-quadruples in cells.
DNA and RNA G-quadrupplexes can self-biotinylate via their intrinsic ability to complex hemin, and that this self-biointylation occurs with good efficiency, good selectivity and good sensitivity.
